A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LVLM-Count. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original counting experiments, component ablations, Penguin threshold experiments, and qualitative application results.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, full-test-set ablations, and qualitative counting experiments, including results retained from v1.

M1.justification: V2 standardizes the described divider on the existing automatic x-axis clustering approach, omitting the alternative equidistant/two-axis schemes and Real-ESRGAN super-resolution step. The core four-stage GroundingDINO/SAM, object-aware A*, and LVLM counting pipeline remains.

E1.justification: The Penguin mixed-site/separate-site study and adverse-weather detection example in v1 Appendix E disappear, narrowing environmental-monitoring test coverage; a qualitative penguin application remains. FSC-147, TallyQA, Emoji-Count, and PASCAL VOC are retained. PASCAL VOC's move into the main text is not new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V2 removes VLCounter from FSC-147, GPT-4o counting segmentation masks from FSC-147/TallyQA/Emoji-Count, and DAVEprm from TallyQA/Emoji-Count/PASCAL VOC while retaining DAVEprm on FSC-147. It adds an FSC-147 GroundingREC row marked not trained on that dataset and a segmentation-mask-count baseline on PASCAL VOC. Comparator membership changes across all four benchmarks.

E3.justification: Appendix A expands from 116 sampled FSC-147 images to the full 1,190-image test set. FSC-147 and Emoji-Count follow the revised automatic division procedure. Figure 18 changes count intervals from boundaries 20/100/300/800 to 20/80/160/320, and PASCAL VOC gains tolerance-accuracy metrics. Emoji generation changes from six categories to up to six; this reported revision does not establish that the data were regenerated.

E4.justification: The component ablation is expanded but loses its super-resolution arm. V2 removes the alternative division comparisons and the entire Penguin detection-threshold sensitivity study, including its failure demonstrations. It replaces v1's explicit ski-counting failure case with successful FSC-147 examples, adds a PASCAL VOC case, and revises the count-range analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three trials for base LVLM and LVLM-Count table results and average Figure 2 over three trials. Neither introduces seed identities, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced: LVLM-Count's FSC-147 MAE with GPT-4o changes from 16.23 to 19.24, and its Emoji-Count MAE with Gemini changes from 14.35 to 11.37. These accompany procedural changes, preventing same-setting performance interpretations. Ablation results, plots, and qualitative counts change; Penguin results disappear and PASCAL tolerance accuracies are added. Retained TallyQA and PASCAL VOC LVLM scores match.

T1.justification: The A* graph construction, count aggregation, and accuracy definitions retain the same mathematics; no theorems or proofs are added. V2's explicit 3-by-3 neighborhood clarifies the neighboring-pixel graph already described in v1.

C1.justification: V1 broadly claims the first method dividing images without cutting target objects; v2 qualifies this novelty claim with targets specified by a text prompt. The main training-free, open-world counting and Emoji-Count benchmark contributions remain, while the abstract foregrounds the already-existing double-counting prevention mechanism.

C2.justification: V2 retains the zero-count hallucination limitation but removes substantive discussions of context loss, extreme-density/resolution problems, and missed detections from v1 Section 5 and Appendix E. Figure 18's caption narrows the rapidly increasing advantage to GPT-4o. The new PASCAL accuracy summary also overlooks CountGD's advantage on tolerance metrics in Table 10.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies 415 Emoji-Count image-question pairs and the graph's 3-by-3 neighborhood. It removes GroundingREC's REC-8K checkpoint-provenance footnote, Penguin sampling/threshold details, and super-resolution configuration notes. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands the comparison with earlier divide-and-conquer counting, adds Stahl et al. (2018), and distinguishes image versus feature division and training restrictions. The Real-ESRGAN citation disappears with that component; most related-work coverage remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: method explanations use a more consistent example, related-work discussion expands, the limitations section becomes a conclusion, and PASCAL VOC moves into the main text. Appendices are extensively reordered, with most figures collected after their explanatory text.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3–6 are redrawn, Figure 2 changes its illustrations and plot, and Figure 18 changes bins and scales. Appendix examples are replaced, resized, and relocated. Tables lose and gain comparator rows; Penguin tables disappear, and a PASCAL tolerance-accuracy table is added.

improvement.justification: The full-test-set ablation and clearer method illustrations improve validation and exposition. However, removing the Penguin robustness study, explicit failure example, and substantive limitations reduces evidence about failure conditions, while the new PASCAL accuracy summary overstates Table 10. These material gains and losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
